title: "Drug enrichment analysis"
format: html
author: Sara Gosline

The goal of this document is to ask if specific genes up-regulated in patient populations
are correalted with drug response across cancer cell lines.


# Download coderdata
Here we have to download coderdata and then format it

We can then download the latest version of the coderdata dataset, using the following command in the terminal:

```{bash}
#| label: download data
#| warning: FALSE
#| eval: FALSE
coderdata download --local_path '/tmp'
```

## Reticulate
We can now set up `reticulate` to interface with Python from R.


```{r}
#| label: imports-and-setup
#| warning: FALSE

# r libraries
library(reticulate)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
library(dplyr)
library(patchwork)
library(GSVA) ##do to the enrichment statistics

# path setupd
data_dir <- "/tmp/"

#wd <- tempdir()
#setwd(wd)
reticulate::use_virtualenv('r-reticulate')
reticulate::import("coderdata")

# defines the python environment to use
py_require("coderdata")

# import the coderdata package from python
cd <- import("coderdata")


```

Once we have loaded the `coderdata` package, we can check the version and list the 
available datasets to confirm that we have the correct version and datasets available.
```{r}
#| label: confirm-version-and-datasets
cd$version()
cd$list_datasets()
```

## Drug data import
Now we are ready to load the datasets and format them for analysis. We will load the
 cell line datasets to load the relevant experimental,
drug, proteomic, and transcriptomic data for each dataset.

Note how this is done using the `reticulate` functionality to call Python functions from R via `cd$load(...)` and `datasets[[name]]$format(...)`.

```{r}
#| label: load-datasets
#| warning: FALSE
#| echo: FALSE


#datasetnames <- c("ccle", "ctrpv2", "prism", "gdscv1", "gdscv2", "nci60")
#datasets <- list()

ds <- cd$load('beataml',local_path = data_dir)
```

# Gene and protein list import

Next we have to collect the genes and proteins that we are interested in. 

```{r}
#| label: load gene lists
#| warning: FALSE

genelists <- readr::read_csv('~/Downloads/combined.csv') |>
    dplyr::mutate(direction = ifelse(logFC<0, 'down','up')) |>
    subset(adj.P.Val <0.05)

##now break them up by name and direction
listnames <- unique(genelists$Contrast)

txtab <- subset(genelists, OmicsType=='TX')|>
  subset(abs(logFC)>1) 
#    dplyr::group_by(Contrast, direction) |> #
#    dplyr::mutate(genelist = paste(gene_symbol, collapse=','))|> 
#    select(Contrast,direction, genelist)|> unique()

pxtab <- subset(genelists, OmicsType=='PX')|>
  subset(abs(logFC)>1) 
#    dplyr::group_by(Contrast, direction) |> 
#    dplyr::mutate(genelist = paste(gene_symbol, collapse=','))|> 
#    select(Contrast,direction, genelist)|> unique()

txlists <- c()
pxlists <- c()
for(li in listnames){
    txlists[[li]] <- list(up = txtab[txtab$Contrast==li&txtab$direction=='up',]$gene_symbol,
                          down = txtab[txtab$Contrast==li&txtab$direction=='down',]$gene_symbol)
    pxlists[[li]] <- list(up = pxtab[pxtab$Contrast==li&pxtab$direction=='up',]$gene_symbol,
                          down = pxtab[pxtab$Contrast==li&pxtab$direction=='down',]$gene_symbol)  
}

#now let's add in the lists from the paper

txlists[['hox']] <- list(up = c('HOXA5','HOXA6','HOXA7','HOXB3','HOXB4','HOXB5','MEIS1','PBX3'))
pxlists[['hox']] <- list(up=c('HOXA10','HOXB4','MESI1','PBX3'), down=c('PROM1','CD34'))

listnames <- c(listnames, 'hox')

```

## RNA based enrichment


```{r}
#| label: RNA based enrichment
#| warning: FALSE
#| echo: FALSE

##load in coderdata file. source from drug-enrichment branch
source("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PNNL-CompBio/coderdata/refs/heads/drug-enrichment-stats/scripts/coderdata_drug_rank.R")

convert_genes <- function(genelist, genemapping){
  res <- genemapping[genemapping$other_id%in%genelist,]|>
    rbind(genemapping[genemapping$genee_symbol%in%genelist,])
 # if(nrow(res) > 0)
    print(paste('converting',length(genelist),'genes to',length(unique(res$entrez_id)),'entrez ids'))
  return(unique(res$entrez_id))
}

##this collects the scores for each list and each dataset
 ex <- ds$format("experiments", shape = "wide", metrics = "fit_auc")
   erange <- ex|>group_by(improve_drug_id)|>
    summarize(range = max(fit_auc) - min(fit_auc)) |>
    subset(range > 0.5)
  ex<- ex|>subset(improve_drug_id%in%erange$improve_drug_id)
 tx <- ds$format("transcriptomics",shape = "matrix", metrics = "transcripomics")
 px <- ds$format('proteomics', shape = 'matrix', metrics = 'proteomics')

rna.results <- lapply(txlists, function(ls){
    rank_coderdata_drugs(
      omics_matrix = t(tx),
      experiment_data = ex,
      signatures = list(up = convert_genes(ls$up, ds$genes),
                          down = convert_genes(ls$down, ds$genes)),
     #drug_data = datasets[[ds]]$drugs,
    # adjust_scope = 'global',
     modality = "transcriptomics",
     method = "ssgsea",
     association = "spearman"
  )})

 
 #now we can extract the ranks we need to compare acros datasets
 rna.ranks <- do.call(rbind, lapply(listnames, function(ls) {
          rna.results[[ls]]$ranking|>
          mutate(listname = ls) |>
           mutate(dataset = 'beataml') 
           }))

#we can also use scores to plot the promising results
rna.scores <- do.call(rbind, lapply(listnames, function(ls){
      return(rna.results[[ls]]$scores|>
          mutate(listname = ls) |>
           mutate(dataset = 'beataml'))
    }))|>
          left_join(ex)

          
```



## Protein based enrichment

Now we can collect the same thing for proteins

```{r}
#| label: protein enrichment
#| error: FALSE
#| warning: FALSE
#| echo: FALSE


##this collects the scores for each list and each dataset
 prot.results <- lapply(pxlists, function(ls){
    res=NULL
    try(res <-rank_coderdata_drugs(
      omics_matrix = t(px),
      experiment_data = ex,
      signatures = list(up = convert_genes(ls$up, ds$genes),
                          down = convert_genes(ls$down, ds$genes)),
     #drug_data = datasets[[ds]]$drugs,
     #adjust_scope = 'global',
     modality = "proteomics",
     method = "ssgsea",
     association = "spearman"
  ))
  return(res)
  })

 
 #now we can extract the ranks we need to compare acros datasets
 prot.ranks <- do.call(rbind, lapply(listnames, function(ls) {
       res<- prot.results[[ls]]$ranking
       if(!is.null(res))
        res|>
          mutate(listname = ls) |>
           mutate(dataset = 'beataml') 
           }))

#we can also use scores to plot the promising results
prot.scores <- do.call(rbind, lapply(listnames, function(ls){
      res <- prot.results[[ls]]$scores
      if(!is.null(res))
        res|>
          mutate(listname = ls) |>
           mutate(dataset = 'beataml')
    }))|>
          left_join(ds$format("experiments", shape = "wide", metrics = "fit_auc"))

```



# Combine results 
Let's combine and plot top drugs
Now we can use a second script I added to create a mapping of common drug names.
```{bash}
#| eval: FALSE
cd aml_outcomes_disparities/analysis/fig8/
curl https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PNNL-CompBio/coderdata/refs/heads/drug-enrichment-stats/scripts/create_common_drug_names.py > ./create_common_drug_names.py
python create_common_drug_names.py --data-dir='/tmp/'

```
Now we can combine the two and add in the new drug annotation file that we might keep. 

```{r combined results}

drug_names <-readr::read_csv('common_drug_names.csv')

combined.res <- rbind(prot.ranks, rna.ranks) |>
  dplyr::left_join(drug_names)


###list the drugs with an average rank below 10?
ranks <- combined.res |>
    group_by(signature, common_name, listname, modality) |> 
    summarize(mrank = median(rank), ndataset = n_distinct(dataset)) |>
    arrange(mrank)

ranks$common_name <- factor(ranks$common_name, levels = unique(ranks$common_name))

combined.res |>
  subset(p_value < 0.1) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x=common_name, y=rank, size = sensitivity_effect, shape = signature, col=modality))+
  facet_grid(~listname) +
  geom_point() + 
  coord_flip() + 
  ggtitle('Top drugs for Bl vs white')

```

# Menin inhibitor search
Can we look for menin inhibitors specifically?/

```{r}
#| label: menin inibitor

mis <-sapply(c('bleximenib','Enzomenib','Zefamenib','Mezinib','BMF-219','DS-1594','JNJ-75276617','DSP-5336','Revumenib','Ziftomenib'),tolower)

subset(combined.res, common_name%in%mis) |> arrange(desc(sensitivity_effect))

##we find some correlation betwen revumenib and the B+/W+


```

```{r}
#| label: plot signature correlation?

listname='B+_W+'
dirname='up'
mode = 'transcriptomics'

subset(rna.scores, improve_drug_id =='SMI_42186')|>
  subset(signature== 'up') |>
  ggplot(aes(x=fit_auc, y = signature_score, col=listname, group=listname))+ geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method='lm')

```
